root_cause.text: Storing the unsigned long return value of `simple_strtoul()` in an `unsigned int` variable (`clen`) causes silent truncation of Content-Length values exceeding UINT_MAX on 64-bit systems, leading to miscalculation of the SIP message boundary and potential processing of trailing data as a new SIP message.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states the type mismatch and truncation: "sip_help_tcp() parses the SIP Content-Length header with simple_strtoul(), which returns unsigned long, but stores the result in unsigned int clen. On 64-bit systems, values exceeding UINT_MAX are silently truncated before computing the SIP message boundary." The patch changes `clen` to `unsigned long` and adds a boundary check `if (clen > datalen) break;` to reject oversized values.

intent_record.what: Changed declaration of 'clen' from 'unsigned int' to 'unsigned long' and moved it to a separate declaration line.
intent_record.how: The variable 'clen' now has a larger type (unsigned long), allowing it to hold larger values without overflow, which affects arithmetic and comparisons in the function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to break if content length exceeds data length, preventing out-of-bounds access in SIP TCP helper.
intent_record.what: Added a condition `if (clen > datalen) break;` after the existing check for `dptr + matchoff == end` in the loop inside `sip_help_tcp`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this check prevents further processing when the content length (`clen`) exceeds the available data length (`datalen`), breaking out of the outer loop to avoid potential out-of-bounds access or processing incomplete data.
